issues.description: The problem statement uses different attribute names in the textual instructions than in the UML and solution. The textual list ("inscribedStudents" and "guestStudents") differs from the UML and solution which use "numberOfInscribedStudents" and "numberOfGuestStudents". This naming inconsistency can confuse students about the exact field names and the corresponding getter/setter method names they must implement (and may lead to failing tests if students follow the textual names instead of the UML/tests).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across the problem statement and UML. Update the textual description to use the exact names from the UML/tests (e.g., "numberOfInscribedStudents" and "numberOfGuestStudents") and explicitly state that students should follow the UML naming and constructor parameter order. Alternatively, mention clearly that the UML names are the canonical names to be used for attributes and corresponding getters/setters.

issues.description: The problem text refers to the student-count attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' while the UML diagram and the solution implementation use the attribute names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents'. This divergence of identifiers for the same conceptual attributes (total inscribed and guest student counts) can cause students to be uncertain which exact names to implement and may confuse them when following the UML/constructor ordering instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute identifiers consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the problem text to use the exact UML/implementation names 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (e.g., change 'inscribedStudents' -> 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' -> 'numberOfGuestStudents'). Alternatively, if shorter names are preferred, update the UML and solution to match 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' and adjust constructor/usage examples accordingly.
